answer:
Don’t hire the agency for this launch. You have $6,000 in monthly recurring revenue, but no demonstrated acquisition channel beyond founder relationships and meetups. Tech coverage might create awareness; it would do little to establish whether subcontractors will buy through a repeatable sales process. The $36,000 commitment is premature.

For the next three months, run one founder-led sales program across the three metros, with events and content supporting it. Budget:

- **$12,000 for outreach:** part-time prospect research, contact data, basic sales tools, and local visits. Founders own discovery calls, demos, and closing.
- **$9,000 for trade-association events:** small, targeted sponsorships with access to actual owners and dispatch managers. Start with one event; fund the others only if it produces qualified conversations.
- **$9,000 for onboarding:** hands-on schedule migration, crew setup, and training to get new customers dispatching real jobs quickly.
- **$6,000 for content:** turn customer-approved workflow demonstrations and measurable results into short LinkedIn posts and YouTube videos used in outreach.

In month one, interview existing customers to identify the strongest buyer profile, purchase trigger, and demonstrated benefit. Build a list of 200 matching subcontractors, divided across the metros, and begin personalized outreach.

In month two, concentrate on the best-performing segment, run the first event, and document objections and onboarding friction. In month three, repeat what produces paying, active customers.

Aim for 10–15 additional customers, tracking acquisition cost, founder hours, sales cycle, activation, and cancellations. At 80% gross margin, $400 monthly pricing supports roughly $3,840 acquisition cost for a 12-month payback.

Assuming customer acquisition is the launch’s purpose, reconsider PR only after this process works—or when a specific publication demonstrably reaches your buyers.
